cases.title: Life-threatening haemoptysis
cases.stem: A patient with bronchiectasis has large-volume haemoptysis and a falling haemoglobin. CTA shows hypertrophied bronchial arteries.

questions.question: Which arterial territory is the most likely initial embolisation target?
options: Bronchial and relevant non-bronchial systemic arteries
questions.explanation: The systemic bronchial circulation is the most common source of severe haemoptysis.

questions.question: Before embolising a bronchial artery, which branch must be actively sought because inadvertent embolisation can cause a catastrophic complication?
questions.explanation: Recognition of spinal arterial supply is critical to avoid spinal cord ischaemia.
questions.imageFile: Lung - Therapeutic Bronchial Artery Embolization With Spherical Microspheres (49160126541).jpg

questions.question: Which embolic material is commonly suitable for distal bronchial artery embolisation?
options: Iodinated contrast as the embolic agent
questions.explanation: Particles are widely used for bronchial artery embolisation; exact choice depends on anatomy and operator strategy.

questions.question: Why can haemoptysis recur after technically successful embolisation?
options: Recanalisation or recruitment of new systemic collaterals
The underlying lung disease is always cured
Recurrence is caused only by pneumothorax
questions.explanation: Persistent underlying disease may lead to recanalisation or development of new collateral arterial supply.

questions.question: What is a key angiographic safety principle during bronchial artery embolisation?
options: Avoid embolisation if a spinal arterial branch cannot be safely excluded or protected
Always use the largest particles available
Embolise the pulmonary artery first in every case
Ignore collateral supply once one bronchial artery is treated
questions.explanation: Identification of spinal arterial supply is critical because non-target embolisation can cause spinal cord ischaemia.

cases.title: Percutaneous ablation of a liver metastasis
cases.stem: A patient has a solitary small liver metastasis, away from the hilum, and is selected for image-guided thermal ablation.

questions.question: What is the oncological objective of percutaneous thermal ablation?
options: Destroy the tumour with an adequate ablation margin when feasible
questions.explanation: The aim is complete tumour destruction together with an adequate circumferential margin when anatomy allows.

questions.question: A lesion lies close to vulnerable bowel. Which adjunct may improve safety?
options: Hydrodissection or another protective displacement technique
questions.explanation: Hydrodissection can physically separate heat-sensitive structures from the ablation zone.

questions.question: Which phenomenon can reduce radiofrequency ablation efficacy adjacent to a large vessel?
questions.explanation: Blood flow in a large vessel can dissipate thermal energy and reduce tissue heating.

questions.question: Which immediate imaging finding supports technical success?
options: The ablation zone completely covers the tumour with an adequate margin and no residual enhancing tumour
questions.explanation: Complete coverage and absence of residual viable enhancement support successful ablation.

questions.question: When technically feasible, what ablation margin is generally sought around a liver metastasis to reduce local tumour progression?
options: A circumferential safety margin beyond the visible tumour
Only the tumour centre needs treatment
A margin confined to the portal vein lumen
questions.explanation: Ablation should encompass the tumour plus an adequate circumferential margin when anatomy permits.

questions.question: In severe malignant superior vena cava obstruction, venous stenting can provide:
options: Rapid relief of venous obstruction in selected patients
questions.explanation: Stenting can relieve venous congestion rapidly while oncological treatment addresses the underlying cause.

questions.question: A transhepatic portal venous approach may be used for:
options: Selected portal venous interventions when other routes are unsuitable
questions.explanation: Transhepatic access provides a percutaneous route to the portal venous system for selected procedures.

questions.question: Percutaneous drainage is usually appropriate for an intra-abdominal abscess when:
options: The collection is clinically significant and safely accessible
Every collection is less than 5 mm
There is no infection or symptom
It consists only of normal bowel gas
questions.explanation: Image-guided drainage is effective for many clinically important accessible collections.

questions.question: During drainage of an infected collection, which principle reduces septic complications?
questions.explanation: Gentle manipulation and effective drainage reduce the risk of forcing infected material into the circulation.

questions.question: An inferior vena cava filter is mainly considered when:
options: There is a selected indication such as acute VTE with a major contraindication to anticoagulation
questions.explanation: IVC filters are not routine and should be reserved for specific clinical indications.

questions.question: When crossing a chronic arterial occlusion, the choice between intraluminal and subintimal techniques depends on:
options: Lesion anatomy, length, calcification and re-entry strategy
questions.explanation: Crossing strategy is determined by lesion morphology, access and available re-entry options.

questions.question: Which complication is specific to prostatic artery embolisation?
options: Non-target embolisation to vesical, rectal or penile branches
questions.explanation: Complex pelvic anastomoses create a recognised risk of non-target embolisation.

questions.question: Valid informed consent for an IR procedure should include:
options: Relevant benefits, material risks and reasonable alternatives
A statement that complications are impossible
questions.explanation: Consent should provide the information required for an informed decision, including alternatives and important risks.

questions.question: For a small renal tumour being considered for percutaneous ablation, which factor most strongly influences technical planning?
options: Tumour size, location and proximity to vulnerable structures
questions.explanation: Size and anatomical relationships determine access, modality, protective manoeuvres and expected margins.

questions.question: Percutaneous ablation of a painful bone metastasis may be combined with cementoplasty when the aim is to:
options: Treat tumour-related pain and improve structural support in selected lesions
questions.explanation: Ablation can address painful tumour while cement augmentation may provide mechanical stabilisation in selected cases.
